subject: Chemistry
title: King Cobra Venom: Neurotoxic Strike
description: A quick win: understand King Cobra Venom: Neurotoxic Strike.

hook.text: A king cobra delivers enough venom in one bite to kill an elephant—or 20 humans.

buildup.text: Its venom contains alpha-neurotoxins that bind to acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction.

discovery.text: Once blocked, nerve signals can't reach muscles. Paralysis begins at the bite and spreads to the diaphragm.

twist.text: The venom also contains enzymes that break down cell membranes, causing massive tissue destruction around the bite.

climax.text: Antivenom works by providing antibodies that bind and neutralize the toxins before they reach nerve receptors.

punchline.text: Blocks nerves, dissolves tissue. One bite delivers a chemical arsenal.

quiz.question: How does king cobra venom cause paralysis?
options: Neurotoxins block acetylcholine receptors so nerves can't signal muscles
It thickens the blood until it stops flowing
It attacks the spinal cord directly

details.summary: The king cobra delivers massive volumes of neurotoxic venom that blocks postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at neuromuscular junctions. A single bite can deliver enough venom to kill an elephant, making it the largest venomous snake and one of the most medically significant.
details.whyItMatters: King cobra venom research has produced a pain medication called ohanin. Understanding its neurotoxins improved the design of drugs targeting acetylcholine receptors for neurological conditions.
takeaways: King cobras deliver the largest venom volume of any snake per bite
The venom blocks acetylcholine receptors causing respiratory paralysis
Venom peptides are being developed into novel pain medications

faq.question: How does king cobra venom differ from viper venom chemically?
faq.answer: King cobra venom is primarily neurotoxic, targeting the nervous system to cause paralysis. Viper venoms are typically hemotoxic, destroying red blood cells and tissues. This fundamental difference means they require different-specific antivenoms and produce different clinical symptoms.

faq.question: Can a king cobra bite kill a full-grown elephant?
faq.answer: Yes. A king cobra can inject up to seven milliliters of venom in a single bite, enough to kill an Asian elephant within hours. However, king cobras rarely encounter elephants. Their primary threat is to humans in Southeast Asian rural communities.
